profile.name: Sigrika
profile.review:
Sigrika is a 5-star Aero Gauntlets DPS character who specializes in the Echo Skill damage archetype, similar to characters like Phrolova and Galbrena. Much like Galbrena, she gets up close and personal to deal high-damaging Aero blows to enemies; but unlike her, Sigrika doesn’t focus on entering an enhanced state to deal her damage; instead, she builds up to a Forte Skill in order to blow enemies away. Let’s look into how to do exactly that:

Key Mechanics

Sigrika’s kit focuses on generating and consuming Runes via Heavy Attacks in order to cast her Forte Skill. She does this via her Basic Attacks, Intro, and Ultimate, all of which are related to Rune generation. Essentially, Sigrika can generate one Rune after performing a full Basic Attack chain. However, this can be upgraded to 2 Runes per chain if she has cast her Intro or Ultimate within the past 20 seconds. In most rotations, one of these Heavy Attacks will be using 2 of the same runes and the other will be using 2 different rune types, though it’s possible to do more/do 2 runes of different types twice if you optimize Sigrika’s rotations. Each rune type influences what Heavy Attack is performed. This is similar to Phrolova’s Forte Basics and Forte Skills.

Sigrika’s Runes gained via her enhanced Basic Attack (which is indicated by the glow on the Basic Attack button after a full Basic Chain) will generate Runes used to stagnate enemies, while Runes gained via her enhanced Skill (indicated by the glow on the Skill button in a similar fashion) will generate Runes used to group enemies.

Sigrika’s special Heavy Attacks can be used if she has any two or more Runes. If two  Runes of the same type are present (this will be the case after her Intro), then the actual effect, depending on the Rune type selected, will take place. However, due to the nature of her Ultimate generating two opposite-type Runes, the next Heavy Attack will simply deal higher damage while having no extra effects instead.

Finally, once two Heavy Attacks were used and 4 Runes were consumed, holding her Skill button will cast her big Forte Skill nuke, ending her rotation. 

Practical Gameplay & Related Mechanics

Given her Key Mechanics explained above, we can come up with a simple rotation where Sigrika casts a full Basic Attack chain after Intro, casts a Heavy Attack, casts her Ultimate, redoes a full Basic Attack chain into a Heavy, and then she’s ready to use her Forte Skill and Outro. Very easy to understand and execute. However, Sigrika has other mechanics that are important to keep in mind when playing her in practice.

First of all, if she needs to dodge out of the way of enemies, it’s not a problem. Her dodge counter works so that the next attack that comes after it is a Basic Attack 4, which means she can easily generate Runes quickly after dodging an enemy attack to ensure a smooth rotation. 

Secondly, it’s worth noting Sigrika has mechanics that discourage swapping, since she’d not only lose out on team Outro Buffs, but also her own Aero and Echo skill damage buff only applies to the active character on-field (this is given via her Inherent Skills and depends on the amount of Echo Skill casts in the team), and she will also lose out on a significant amount of DMG Amplification built into her Forte on all of her most damaging abilities.

Thirdly and finally, Sigrika can always change up her rotations to alter the rune types that are generated, or simply generate more Runes than is necessary for her rotation to be performed. Rotations aren’t always unidimensional and can be altered if properly optimized.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Sigrika is a strong DPS, but this comes at a cost. Almost all of her damage is Echo Skill DMG, which basically no character can buff aside from Qiuyuan or Lucilla. To make matters worse, Sigrika has 3 different layers of built-in mechanics that depend on the amount of Echo Skills cast in the team, built into her Forte and Inherent Skills. They each give significant amounts of DMG Bonus and DMG Amplification on her highest-damaging abilities. This makes her performance very reliant on Qiuyuan or Lucilla, as her strongest alternative is playing alongside Lynae and Mornye who obviously really pale in comparison.

Overall, Sigrika’s reliance on Qiuyuan or Lucilla as teammates is very much felt, and she is stranded for other teammate options currently due to the amount of mechanics she has that are tied to having a higher amount of Echo Skill casts than normal in the team, as well as her more exclusive damage type which has no viable permanently accessible options. While she definitely has strong potential, her opportunity cost should also be kept in mind, considering she lacks strong F2P weapon and teammate alternatives.

In conclusion, while Sigrika is a super strong DPS, she has a major flaw in regards to opportunity cost, which makes her valuable or not, depending on your account and pull plans. But if you give Sigrika the conditions she needs to shine, she’ll absolutely serve you as one of the strongest DPS in the game. Her modern damage numbers are nothing to scoff at, as she is easily one of the strongest WhiWa DPS thanks to her ridiculous AoE and fast rotation. Plus, she is one of the strongest in ToA/Matrix too,  all this so long as she is provided with the sufficient amount of investment and surrounded by the proper teammates.
profile.pros:
• One of the best overall DPS performances in the game within her best team, given the right amount of investment. One of the strongest WhiWa DPS by a big margin and an insane ToA/Matrix DPS too;

  • Can buff the team’s Aero and Echo damage, providing extra synergies;

  • Very high substat scaling. The better her build, the more she stands out from other characters that normally would be on par with her.
profile.cons: • Lacks good F2P teammates and F2P weapons. Basically a necessity to at least have Qiuyuan or Lucilla as a readily available teammate, and her Signature is a desirable upgrade as well to get her up to the top-level performance she can output.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Sigrika’s kit focus is around generating her Runes as quickly as possible in order to cast her high-damaging Forte skill and end her rotation. For this, she only has one way to go about it: cast Basic Attacks following her Intro and Ultimate. We can hence come up with a very simple rotation as follows:

Echo Timing

Cast Summon at any point in her rotation.

Standard Rotation

  • Intro

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Cancel animation endlag via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Chain Whip (Cancel animation on first hit via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Cancel animation endlag via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Outburst (Cancel animation on cast via Hold Skill)

  • Hold Skill: Learn My True Name

  • Outro

Double Outburst

In more advanced Hypercarry Sigrika setups, there will be significant headroom for Sigrika to extend her team’s rotation since she and her team will rotate very quickly. As a result, with Qiuyuan/Lucilla (in Quickswap)+Shorekeeper, where the team rotation is fast, it’s possible for her to extend her own rotation in such a way that she takes advantage of the extra rotation time provided to her by building up to 2 of her stronger Outburst Forte Heavies (2 different Runes on cast), by changing her Opener and Loop, like so:

Double Outburst Opener

  • Intro

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Cancel animation endlag via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Chain Whip (Cancel animation on first hit via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Cancel animation endlag via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Outburst (Cancel animation on cast via Hold Skill)

  • Hold Skill: Learn My True Name

  • Skill

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Interrupt animation on cast via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Skill: BIG BOOMY BOOM! (Swap when Rune is generated)

  • Outro

Double Outburst Loop

  • Intro

  • Heavy: Outburst (Cancel animation on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Skill: Soliskin to the Aid

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Cancel animation endlag via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Outburst (Cancel animation on cast via Hold Skill)

  • Hold Skill: Learn My True Name

  • Ultimate

  • Skill

  • Basic 3

  • Basic 4

  • Basic: Elucidated (Swap out of animation endlag)

  • Outro

It is, however, worth noting the above rotation isn’t worth executing if the full team using the Standard Rotation already has you taking 25s (or very close to it). The above rotation is a rotation extension if there is time to spare, not a strict upgrade, and is only for players willing to fully optimize fast team loops.

skills.name: One, Two, Three
skills.description:
Basic Attack

  • Perform up to 4 consecutive attacks, dealing Aero DMG.

  • Enter Decipher state for 5s after casting Basic Attack Stage 4. This effect ends early if Sigrika is switched off the field.

  • When Sigrika has at least 50 points of Full Stop, her Basic Attack cycle starts from Stage 2.

Basic Attack - Elucidated

  • In the Decipher state, press Normal Attack on the ground to cast Basic Attack - Elucidated, dealing Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

  • Leave the Decipher state upon casting this skill.

Heavy Attack

  • Consume STA to attack the target, dealing Aero DMG. Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Heavy Attack to cast Basic Attack Stage 2.

Mid-air Attack

  • Consume STA to perform Plunging Attack, dealing Aero DMG.

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Plunging Attack to cast Basic Attack Stage 2.

Dodge Counter

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge on the ground to attack the target, dealing Aero DMG.

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Dodge Counter to cast Basic Attack Stage 4.

Dodge Counter - Decipher

  • In the Decipher state, press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge on the ground to cast Dodge Counter - Decipher to attack the target, dealing Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

  • Leave the Decipher state upon casting this skill.

Mid-air Dodge Counter

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge in mid-air to attack the target, dealing Aero DMG.

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after casting Mid-air Dodge Counter to cast Basic Attack Stage 2.

skills.name: Royan Close Quarters Combat
skills.description:
BOOMY BOOM!

  • Attack the target, dealing Aero DMG.

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after casting BOOMY BOOM! to cast Basic Attack Stage 3.

BIG BOOMY BOOM!

  • While in the Decipher state, press Resonance Skill on the ground to cast BIG BOOMY BOOM!, dealing Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

  • Leave the Decipher state upon casting this skill.

Soliskin to the Aid

  • While in the Decipher state, with at least 50 points of Full Stop, press Resonance Skill on the ground to cast Soliskin to the Aid, dealing Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

  • Leave the Decipher state upon casting this skill.

skills.name: Where Trust Leads Me!
skills.description:
Deal Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG). Gain Divergent for 20s.

Divergent

  • The next time Sigrika obtains a Rune, she additionally obtains a Rune of the opposite type and removes Divergent.

  • When Sigrika holds Divergent and Convergent at the same time, Convergent takes priority.

  • When Sigrika holds 100 points of Full Stop, Divergent doesn't take effect.

skills.name: Within Infinity's Embrace
skills.description:
Heavy Attack - Schemata of Runes

  • Hold Normal Attack to consume two Runes and cast Heavy Attack - Schemata of Runes, dealing Aero DMG. Based on the types of the Runes consumed, Sigrika gains the following effects:

    • When consuming Rune: Trust and Rune: Answer, this skill gains the effect of Runic Outburst.

    • When consuming two Runes: Trust, this skill gains the effect of Runic Chain Whip.

    • When consuming two Runes: Answer, this skill gains the effect of Runic Soliskin.

  • When consuming Runes, if Sigrika holds at least 30 points of Soliskin Vitality, consume 30 points to increase the DMG Multipliers of the current Runic Outburst, Runic Chain Whip, and Runic Soliskin by 50%. Obtain a stack of Innate Gift?.

  • When consuming Runes, if Soliskin Vitality is lower than 30 points, consume all Soliskin Vitality. Every 10 points of Soliskin Vitality consumed grants the current Runic Outburst, Runic Chain Whip, and Runic Soliskin 15% DMG Amplification.

  • Heavy Attack - Schemata of Runes deals Echo Skill DMG.

Runic Outburst

  • Deal Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Runic Chain Whip

  • Stagnate nearby targets and deal Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Runic Soliskin

  • Pull in nearby targets and deal Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Forte Circuit - Learn My True Name

  • When Full Stop reaches 100 points, if Forte Circuit - Learn My True Name is not on Cooldown, press Resonance Skill to cast Resonance Skill - BOOMY BOOM! or Resonance Skill - Soliskin to the Aid. Hold Resonance Skill to consume all Full Stop to cast Forte Circuit - Learn My True Name, dealing Aero DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Innate Gift?

  • Sigrika can hold up to 2 stacks of Innate Gift?. Each stack grants Runic Outburst, Runic Chain Whip, Runic Soliskin and Forte Circuit - Learn My True Name 30% DMG Amplification.

  • This effect ends after Sigrika casts Forte Circuit - Learn My True Name or is switched off the field.

Rune

  • Sigrika holds up to 4 Runes. Without Full Stop, Sigrika can only hold up to 2 Runes. When Sigrika gains a new Rune at max capacity, the existing Runes shift one slot to the left, removing the leftmost Rune. With at least 50 points of Full Stop, Sigrika can hold 2 additional Runes.

  • Hitting a target with Basic Attack - Elucidated or Dodge Counter - Decipher grants one Rune: Trust.

  • Hitting a target with Resonance Skill - BIG BOOMY BOOM! or Resonance Skill - Soliskin to the Aid grants one Rune: Answer.

Full Stop

  • After casting Heavy Attack - Schemata of Runes, gain 50 points of Full Stop.

Soliskin Vitality

  • When any nearby Resonators in the team cast Echo Skill, Sigrika gains 10 points of Soliskin Vitality, up to 60 points. Echoes with the same name can only trigger this effect once. Casting Outro Skill - In This Very Moment resets the record of Echo triggering this effect.

skills.name: True Names Aligned
skills.description:
When any nearby Resonators in the team cast Echo Skill, Sigrika gains a stack of Blessing of Runes, up to 6 stacks. Echoes with the same name can only trigger this effect once.

This effect resets upon a lineup change.

Blessing of Runes

  • When Blessing of Runes reaches 6 stacks. Sigrika gains an additional 30% increase in Aero DMG Bonus and Echo Skill DMG Bonus.

  • For every 1% of Sigrika's Energy Regen over 125%, Sigrika gains 2% Echo Skill DMG Bonus for up to 50%.

skills.name: In This Very Moment
skills.description:
Attack the target, deal Aero DMG equal to 795% of Sigrika's ATK. Gain 2 stacks of Encapsulated for 30s.

weapons.Comment: Sigrika's Signature weapon is the only one to give her the stats she desires, being a mix of high Base ATK, CRIT DMG, Echo Skill DMG Amplification and providing extra DEF Ignore to Aero DMG, making it the de facto best choice for her by a good amount.

Zani's Signature weapon provides the same base stats as her Signature alongside an extra 8% DEF Ignore when Sigrika casts her Basic Attacks, making for a small extra boost compared to the alternatives below it.
Calculation also applicable to Tragicomedy and Daybreaker's Spine. The best permanent option for Sigrika which is just an ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for her.
Another ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick which provides 12% All-Attribute DMG Bonus instead of ATK, making it a bit worse than the above options.

This weapon gives too much CRIT Rate when factoring in Sigrika's own kit buffs, and also has a lower Base ATK than the above options, which makes it perform worse than them as an ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Sigrika.
While this weapon provides massive ATK and Energy Regen stats, it lacks the CRIT stat that the weapons above it have, making it a worse option overall.

This Battle Pass exclusive is the best 4-star option Sigrika has by a tiny margin thanks to the CRIT and ATK stats it provides, but due to a much lower Base ATK than all other 5-star choices it pales in comparison to them.

Best F2P no-gacha option for Sigrika, of which she can enable the passive thanks to Ciaccona being on her team in our calculations. Without the passive activated, it will perform worse than listed but still be an acceptable temporary choice. Still, try to chase 5-star options like Pulsation Bracer if you can to get good performance out of Sigrika.

echoes.Comment: Grants Sigrika a very easy to access 20% CRIT Rate and 25% Aero DMG Bonus, making for a simple choice of the best stat bonuses she can get from an Echo set.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Simple Summon Echo, can be used at any point in the rotation and grants 12% Aero DMG Bonus as well as 20% Echo Skill DMG Bonus when equipped in the Main Slot. A no-brainer for Sigrika.

echoStats.Name: sigrika
echoStats.Substats: Energy Regen (Until Satisfied) > CRIT DMG = CRIT Rate > Energy Regen (Until 150%) > ATK% > ATK
echoStats.Comments: After CRIT stats are acquired and your base Energy Regen requirement is met, the best idea is to go for 150% ER (or close to it). Ideally, this happens through substats and double ATK% mainstats. However, this is a very difficult build to get. In those cases, an ER mainstat can be considered - keep in mind ER only gives damage benefits past 125%.

skillPriority.Order: Forte Circuit, Res. Liberation, Basic Attack, Intro Skill, Res. Skill
skillPriority.Comments: Intro and Skill practically don't matter and should be skipped when levelling. Forte is by far the most important.

teams.Name: Best Team
teams.Comments: Phrolova can be considered stronger for AoE multi-wave encounters like Whimpering Wastes. Generally privilege other Support options in single-wave encounters.

teams.Name: Alternative Teams
teams.Comments: Mornye should only be used alongside Lynae, Aero Rover should only be used alongside Ciaccona.

synergies.Comment: These are the best buffers Sigrika has to increase her damage. Qiuyuan and Lucilla provide the Echo Skill casts and Echo Skill damage buffs Sigrika desires to take full leverage of her kit, making them the strongest synergies by a lot and a staple of all top Sigrika teams. Ciaccona is the best third slot buffer with Qiuyuan thanks to her ability to buff party-wide Aero DMG and provide Aero RES Shred with her Signature, though without her Signature Shorekeeper, particularly with Lucilla, will be privileged. She can also work in the second slot alongside Shorekeeper or Aero Rover. Finally, Lynae is the alternative if you lack the other options thanks to her very generalized buffing capabilities.

Phrolova has a particular synergy with Sigrika, since they function in a very similar way and can both take advantage of Qiuyuan's extra Echo Skill casts at the same time to deal lots of damage together. Sigrika has the ability to buff Phrolova a little bit with her Inherent Skill but it doesn't amount to much, it's mostly just the two working well with Qiuyuan to deal high damage in tandem. Works fantastically well for Whimpering Wastes and can be considered for single-target encounters if Phrolova lacks her ideal teammates like Cantarella.

Some of the best third slot teammates for Sigrika are listed here. Shorekeeper is generally the strongest choice in a lot of cases thanks to her extra Sustain capabilities compared to Ciaccona and also the fact she doesn't need a Signature weapon to provide close to the fullest extent of her team buffs. Mornye works better than her in tandem with Lynae, Aero Rover works better in tandem with Ciaccona if you use alternative teams to Sigrika's best. Finally, if none of those options are preferred, Verina works generally well as a permanently accessible and very capable Support.
